title: Euphoria
synopsis: You're 20 in East Highland, two years into recovery, working a coffee shop with a sponsor on speed dial. Tonight's meeting is the first you've gone to alone. The town has not gotten quieter.

nodes.text: Church basement. Cheap coffee. You sit on a folding chair early, headphones in. People begin filing in. You see a face you do not want to see: Cassie.

choices.text: Stay; recovery is bigger than your discomfort
Step outside for one minute

nodes.text: She approaches. She is sober too, surprisingly, and she looks like she has cried already today. She says, 'Can we talk after?' You haven't spoken in two years.

choices.text: Agree to talk
Say 'maybe' and see how the hour goes

nodes.text: On the sidewalk you call your sponsor — Ali, who picks up on the second ring even on Tuesdays. He listens. He says, 'You're already doing the work by calling. Go back inside.'

choices.text: Go back inside steadily
Stay outside for the meeting

nodes.text: You share, briefly, that this is your first meeting alone. The room is warm. An older woman named Marsha says 'glad you're here' in the exact way you needed.

choices.text: Stay for fellowship after
Slip out quickly

nodes.text: Cassie's sister Lexi is at the meeting too, in the back, surprising you both. She catches your eye and gives a small, kind nod. The Howard sisters have, somehow, both ended up in this room.

choices.text: Talk to Lexi first
Talk to both sisters at once

nodes.text: You, Lexi, Cassie, and Marsha sit at a diner counter at 10 p.m. and order pancakes. Cassie cries quietly into hers. Nobody comments. Lexi reaches over and squeezes her hand.

choices.text: Tell Cassie you're glad she's sober
Tell Lexi you're glad she's here too

nodes.text: Wednesday morning. The coffee shop. Your manager Fez is, somehow, kind of a manager now. He gives you the morning shift on purpose so the rest of the day is yours.

choices.text: Tell Fez about the meeting
Stay quiet at work and write later

nodes.text: You keep a notebook. You write the sentence: 'I went to a meeting alone and I came home alone and I did not use.' You read it three times. You realize you have started, slowly, to believe in yourself.

choices.text: Buy a second notebook for the year
Start texting one line a day to Ali

nodes.text: Jules is in town for the week. The first phone call is tentative. The second is honest. The third is, in some way you can't yet name, possible.

choices.text: See her
Wait to see her until you've talked to Ali

nodes.text: Your mom watches you make her coffee in the morning. She does not say much. She doesn't have to. She has, you realize, been working as hard as you, for longer.

choices.text: Tell her you love her plainly
Cook her breakfast in return

nodes.text: Your sister Gia is in high school now. She watches you the way she used to watch the front door at 3 a.m. You realize she is not yet sure you will not relapse. You realize her patience is also love.

choices.text: Take Gia somewhere fun on Saturday
Apologize directly for the years

nodes.text: Two years. Marsha hands you a chip. You almost don't take it because chips have, in the past, felt like jinxes. You take it. You squeeze it in your hand the whole drive home.

choices.text: Pin it on your fridge
Carry it in your pocket every day

nodes.text: Fez tells you he's opening a small bakery. He wants you as the manager. The hours are hard. The job is real. You realize you have been offered, of all things, a future.

choices.text: Accept the job
Negotiate fewer hours so you can keep writing

nodes.text: Six months later the bakery opens. You and Fez and Marsha and Lexi and your mom and Gia are there. There is a small cake. Marsha gives a small speech. Fez almost cries. You almost cry.

choices.text: Take a photo for the year
Just be there

nodes.text: You write — not a book, exactly, but a small collection of essays. You publish one in a magazine. The piece, more than the bakery or the job, makes you feel like a person with a project.

choices.text: Send the essay to Jules
Send it to your sponsor

nodes.text: Jules replies in a long email. She says she's proud of you. She says she's not in a place to come home. She says she'd like to keep writing. You realize, slowly, that not all loves are reunions. Some are just letters.

choices.text: Accept the letters as enough
Plan to visit her in a year, no pressure

nodes.text: Ali, who is dying — you don't know it yet, you'll find out next month — sends you back a one-line text: 'You're writing the version of yourself the rest of us can read.' You frame it.

choices.text: Visit Ali in person next weekend
Send him a long thank-you letter

nodes.text: Five years. You give the chip back at a meeting you sponsor a teenager from. You realize you are now Marsha. You realize this is, finally, a story without an exit.

choices.text: Stay in East Highland
Move; keep the meetings the same

nodes.text: Gia graduates high school. You give the speech at the family dinner. You say plain things. Your mom cries. Gia hugs you longer than usual. You go to bed sober and full and tired in the right way.

choices.text: Keep building the small life
Travel for the first time in your life

nodes.text: Ali is gone. You sit in the meeting in the chair he used to sit in. The room is the same. You are the same and very different. You decide what to do with the rest of the year.

choices.text: Hold the chair in East Highland
Take meetings on the road

nodes.text: You stay. The town gets a little kinder, year over year. You sponsor four people over a decade. Two of them stay sober. Two of them don't. You learn that the score isn't the point. The room is the point.

You travel. Meetings everywhere, surprisingly, work the same way. You write essays from cafés in cities you used to dream about as a teenager. You realize that recovery is portable. So, finally, are you.
